title: The Summit of Cape Reckoning
premise: When a glaciology expedition led by his estranged father's old partner goes silent above the Gorge of Bells, riverboat captain Jude Thackeray is hired—by the man's daughter, Dr. Elena Marsh—to run the last navigable stretch before calving season seals the route. What begins as a rescue becomes an excavation: the missing expedition was hunting proof that Jude's father, long presumed drowned, reached the forbidden source and hid what he found there. As the river narrows and loyalties fracture, Jude must choose between protecting his father's legend and telling the truth that could save them all. In the end, he reaches the source, learns his father died trying to warn others away from a collapsing ice dam, and brings Elena—and the truth—back downriver as the summit finally gives way behind them.
about_author: C. M. Quintana is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight runs on northern rivers. Their writing blends hard-won nautical detail with a cartographer's love for places that resist being mapped.

chapters.title: The Last Charter
chapters.summary: Jude Thackeray, POV. A routine season ends when Dr. Elena Marsh hires his boat for an upriver run to find her missing father's expedition. Jude refuses at first—the upper river killed men he knew—but a debt to Elena's father tips him. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment; the past knocking on a door Jude nailed shut.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Loading the boat, Jude reflects on fifteen years measuring life in river miles since his father's disappearance. Elena proves competent but secretive about the expedition's real cargo. First radio static from upstream—a fragment of a voice Jude almost recognizes. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing in practical routines.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Bells
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The boat threads the gorge where the last expedition's supply cache is found ransacked—not by animals, but cut open deliberately. Elena reveals a partial journal page: her father believed the source held evidence of something buried in the glacier. Emotional beat: dread replacing adventure; trust tested.

chapters.title: Dead Water
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Above the gorge the river braids into shallows; they abandon the boat and take the expedition's abandoned inflatable. They find the first body—frozen upright, holding a radio set to transmit nothing. Jude recognizes the man from his father's crew. Emotional beat: horror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Sheltering in an expedition tent, they read the recovered journals: Jude's father reached the source alive, discovered a meltwater cavity under the ice dam, and tried to turn the team back. The leader refused—the discovery was worth too much. Emotional beat: the father transformed from myth to flawed, brave man.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Map
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They catch up to two surviving expedition members who split the party weeks ago. One, Voss, admits he led the push onward and left the others when the route worsened. He has half a map; the other survivor has the rest—and a rifle. Emotional beat: betrayal made flesh; loyalty vs. truth turns literal.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The glacier groans; the brief window is closing days early. The armed survivor forces the group toward the source against Jude's warnings, and a serac collapse kills him and nearly takes Elena. Jude pulls her from a crevasse. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They reach the forbidden source: a blue chamber beneath the ice where Jude finds his father's final camp—journals, photographs, and a recorded warning about the unstable dam. His father died here, not drowned, sending that warning downstream. Emotional beat: mourning and inheritance reconciled; the truth accepted.

chapters.title: Running the Break
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The dam begins to fail; the only way out is downriver through floodwater no boat should survive. Jude rebuilds the inflatable rig while Voss redeems himself hauling gear, and they launch into the surge. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration fused; every skill Jude owns spent at once.

chapters.title: Downstream Light
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Wrecked but alive, they reach the lower river as the summit collapses behind them into mist. Jude delivers his father's records to the world and, for the first time, stops counting miles—choosing instead to stay, with Elena, where the story began. Emotional beat: release; memory honored, future chosen.
